title: "Physician Exodus from Tunisia: Dynamic Workforce Projections, Retention Policy Counterfactuals, and Economic Evaluation to 2050"

abstract: |
  **Background**: The escalating emigration of physicians from Tunisia poses a structural threat to the sustainability of the public health system, universal health coverage, and regional equity. Since 2021, annual medical departures have exceeded 1,450 doctors per year (~10% of the active workforce), with over 6,000 physicians emigrating between 2021 and 2024.
  
  **Methods**: We developed an empirically grounded, 36-cell discrete-time Markov cohort simulation model with a continuous-time competing-risk hazard matrix engine, integrating the WHO Health Labour Market Framework, a Calibrated Macro-Policy Proportional Hazard Framework, and CHEERS 2022 standards. The baseline active stock at $t_0 = 2020$ was initialized via 2D Iterative Proportional Fitting (IPF) on official census data, adjusting for inactive registrations ($\alpha = 0.88$, yielding $N_0 = 13,477$ practicing doctors). Survey intentions were scaled by specialty-specific realization factors ($\kappa \in [0.25, 0.49]$) and corrected for odds ratio non-collapsibility. Two global scalar calibration parameters were estimated on a 2015–2021 historical training sample ($df = 5$), validated on a 2022–2024 holdout sample, and cross-checked against French (DREES/RPPS) and German (Bundesärztekammer) destination registries ($r = 0.871$). We simulated six policy counterfactuals (2025–2050): Status Quo (SCEN_0), Public Remuneration Reform (+30%, SCEN_1), Hospital Infrastructure Modernization (SCEN_2), Regional Rural Retention Package (SCEN_3), Training Quota Expansion (+15%, SCEN_4), and Comprehensive Synergistic Reform (SCEN_5).
  
  **Results**: Under Status Quo, active domestic physician density collapses strictly and monotonically from 11.4 per 10,000 population in 2020 to 7.7 per 10k by 2050, while the cumulative emigrated diaspora reaches 23,767 physicians abroad (~2.2x the domestic active workforce). Expanding training quotas alone (SCEN_4) exacerbates brain drain (+2,303 additional emigrants), creating >117 Million TND in unrecovered public educational deadweight loss. Hospital infrastructure modernization (SCEN_2) is the most cost-effective single lever ($\text{ICER}_{\text{public}} = 209,137\text{ TND}$ per discounted public physician-year retained). Comprehensive Reform (SCEN_5) maximizes domestic practicing capacity, generating 10,040 discounted public physician-years (15,151 undiscounted) and 4,058 interior physician-years at an $\text{ICER}_{\text{public}}$ of 210,374 TND (discounted net cost of 2,112.1 Million TND, averaging ~84.5 Million TND/year or ~2.8% of the annual health budget). However, because SCEN_5 bundles intake expansion, it results in a net increase in cumulative emigrants abroad ($-361$ deterministic; median $-920$ PSA; 95% CrI: $-1,658$ to $-172$), demonstrating that supply expansion without 100% bonded service mechanically increases gross departures. In 1,000-draw Monte Carlo PSA, SCEN_5 achieves >80% cost-effectiveness probability at willingness-to-pay thresholds above 250,000 TND/physician-year.
  
  **Conclusion**: Supply expansion without retention fails to resolve health workforce depletion and accelerates outward brain drain. A synergistic, multi-attribute policy package combining public salary adjustment, hospital modernization, and regional hardship incentives is macro-fiscally feasible and essential to safeguard Tunisia's health system through 2050.

# Declarations

## Ethics Approval and Consent to Participate
This study is a health workforce demographic simulation and economic evaluation utilizing secondary aggregated administrative registries and published peer-reviewed survey statistics. No individual patient or human subject contact occurred, and all secondary microdata were fully de-identified. Formal institutional ethical review was waived in accordance with Tunisian national research guidelines.

## Consent for Publication
Not applicable.

## Availability of Data and Materials
The complete reproducible modeling pipeline, simulation scripts in R (version 4.4.1), automated test suite, raw and processed data tables, and high-resolution figure generators are publicly available in the project repository.

## Competing Interests
The authors declare that they have no competing financial, personal, or professional interests that could have influenced the design, execution, or reporting of this study.

## Funding
This research received no dedicated external commercial funding. Computational resources were provided by the University of Tunis El Manar.

## Authors' Contributions
FZ and MZ conceptualized the study. FZ designed and programmed the econometric methodology and dynamic Markov simulation model, acquired empirical data, and performed calibration and scenario simulations. FZ and MZ conducted the economic and sensitivity analyses, interpreted the findings, and drafted and critically revised the manuscript. Both authors read and approved the final manuscript.

## Acknowledgements
The authors express their gratitude to the Direction des Études et de la Planification at the Ministère de la Santé de Tunisie, the Institut National de la Statistique (INS), and the Conseil National de l'Ordre des Médecins (CNOM) for making public health workforce statistical reports accessible.
